nodes.title: Vec.push loops into a reserved vector: fill without per-element length stores
nodes.desc: Found by FND-PIPELINE-INSNS (perf annotate, 2026-11-27): the feature pipeline's fill loop 'values = Vec.push(values, i & 65535)' into Vec.with_capacity(n) runs scalar, about 9 instructions per element: a capacity compare branching to the kush_vec_push grow call, the element store, and a store of the length every iteration (mov %rbp,(%r15), 30% of samples). C fills with vector stores. That is roughly 230M of the 520M instructions (C 352M); the map loop is vectorized and the checksum is vectorized with deferred overflow. Lower a counted push loop whose capacity covers the trip count to a check before the loop and a fill loop that writes the length once (or keep the length in a register and write it back on exit and before the grow call), so LLVM can vectorize it. Check with perf stat on benchmarks/languages pipeline.

log.text: Design (not started in code): the per-push length store is by design in push_shadows (memory never stale). LLVM cannot promote it: the grow call clobbers memory and header/elements share one buffer. Plan: version a counted push-only loop on capacity - length >= trip count in the preheader; the copy has no grow path, keeps the length in its shadow and writes it to the header on exit only. Limit to elements without drop glue (a stale length on unwind only leaks) and to loops whose in-loop Vec.len/Vec.get read the shadow or do not occur. Needs a MIR statement that stores a buffer header word (only Rvalue::Buffer reads exist): text, parse, verify, machine, native.
